schemes.description: Teams of up to six Level 3 Physics students, formed by the course organiser, work 9 hours/week for 8 weeks on a physics-related problem set by a client (a local company, or sometimes department staff): e.g. a camera system to film a dishwasher cycle for Procter & Gamble; a calculator for UHV system design for Mantis Vacuum Systems. Each team has a staff consultant, lab space and a £200-300 budget; ends with a short written report and oral presentation to which clients are invited.
schemes.eligible_faculties_programmes: Level 3 Physics students (module listed as Open, cap 84, prerequisite PHYS2641); F300 course page presents it as one of two practical-module options alongside an extended experimental project; also listed for incoming/exchange students 2026/27.
schemes.eligibility_restrictions: Prerequisite PHYS2641 (Laboratory Skills Electronics); capped at 84 places.
schemes.credit_assessment: 20 Durham credits (10 ECTS in 2026/27 incoming handbook); short written report and oral presentation (summative).
schemes.duration: 9 hours/week for 8 weeks in Michaelmas or Epiphany term
schemes.delivery_format: Department-based lab project with client brief, kick-off meeting and final presentation
schemes.project_evidence: Defined client problem with report and presentation outputs (sources 1,2).
schemes.group_evidence: Teams of up to six (4-6) students assembled by the course organiser; joint report and presentation (sources 1,2).
schemes.employer_evidence: Clients supply a ~1 page brief, meet students at the start, may lend equipment, answer queries, may do a mid-project review and are invited to final presentations (source 2); named past clients Procter & Gamble, Cottam Brush, Neue Schule, Mantis Vacuum Systems (source 3). However the module page says problems are set 'by either members of staff from the Department or by local industry' (source 1), so the external share is not established; the F300 programme page says the scenario is presented by an external organisation such as a public body or company (source 4).
schemes.partner_role: Client: supplies brief, meets team, receives final presentation; internal staff-set projects also exist (share not published).
schemes.named_partners: Procter & Gamble, Cottam Brush, Neue Schule, Mantis Vacuum Systems (previous projects page, undated); EDF, Coltraco Ultrasonics, Magnitude Biosciences, Kromek (team project page, undated)
schemes.deliverable: Written report and oral presentation / prototype or analysis for the client
schemes.participation_data: Module cap of 84 students (capacity, not participation).
schemes.unresolved: Share of projects set by external clients vs department staff not published, so C left Unclear. Module page availability reported inconsistently across searches (2024/25 vs 2025/26); currency rests on the 2026/27 incoming-student handbook listing. No dated 2025/26 or 2026/27 client list found. Client page: projects set 'either by Physics staff or by local industry' so external share is not stated as standard (coverage Some projects; C stays Unclear). Past partners named on undated page.

profile_md:
Durham's verified employer-linked group project provision is **distributed across departments rather than institution-wide**, with a small central employer-facing offer. The clearest current routes are two curricular modules: **COMP2281 Software Engineering** (compulsory Year 2 Computer Science teams build a substantial software project in partnership with an external organisation; listed available 2025/26) and **GEOL4091 Earth Sciences into Industry** (optional Level 4 group project in which a client, typically an external organisation, sets the problem and deliverables and receives the groups' presented solution; 60% group report, listed 2025/26).

The **Physics Team Project (PHYS3581)** fits closely (teams of up to six, 8 weeks, client brief, presentation to clients such as Procter & Gamble and Mantis Vacuum Systems) but problems are set by 'staff or local industry', so the external share is unproven. The central **Mini Consultancy Competition** (three-week, employer-set issue, three student teams) is documented only on an employer page, with no student eligibility or dated cohort. Engineering's pair-based **Industrial Problem Solving** live company project is only evidenced to 2019; the year-long Engineering Design team project has industry-professional input but no evidenced client brief. Business School client projects (MBA Strategic Consulting Project, MSc Management Business Project) are mainly individual; MSc Business Analytics projects use client data but their team status is unclear.

No university-wide or compulsory-for-all route was found. Remaining uncertainty: eligibility and currency of the central scheme, arts/social science/health applied projects (search limit reached), and how external clients are used in the Physics and Computer Science projects.
gaps: Search limit reached before checking Participatory Action Research (SOCI43715) and further arts/social science, education, health and law clinic provision. Further departmental instances likely (Engineering design/capstone with Industrial Partnership Committee partners, Biosciences, Psychology, Education). Central Mini Consultancy Competition lacks student-side eligibility, date and cohort evidence. Many sources are undated module/course pages or search-summary paraphrases of them; page contents were not opened directly. Resume pass (2026-10-13, 3 searches): Mini Consultancy student-side selection/team details still not found (employer-side page only: 3 teams, 3 weeks); MSc Business Analytics team vs individual still unconfirmed; PHYS3581 external share not stated.
